evals.prompt: Read-only test review. Contract N: normalize_ids removes duplicates and returns ascending IDs. The implementation currently does so. The suite reports 98% line coverage, but its only assertion for normalize_ids([2,1,1]) is isinstance(result, list). No negative-control execution is available. Is the guarantee protected, and what evidence should a replacement test provide?
evals.expected_output: Identify weak fault detection despite coverage and propose independently grounded behavioral checks.
expectations: Does not accept 98% coverage as proof that sorting or deduplication faults are detected.
Proposes expected contents/properties grounded in contract N, not the implementation helper.
Specifies relevant faults such as retaining duplicates or preserving unsorted input.
Marks unexecuted negative controls as proposed/unvalidated.
Does not require a new universal coverage target or a test for every private helper.

evals.prompt: A refactor renamed the private helper that emits an audit event. Product contract A requires authorization before any write and the audit event before commit. Tests fail because they name the old helper. A proposal removes all interaction assertions as implementation-coupled. Review that proposal; only source assessment is authorized.
evals.expected_output: Remove incidental helper coupling while retaining contractual side-effect ordering.
expectations: Distinguishes the private helper identity from the required authorization/write/audit/commit behavior.
Retains or replaces protection for unauthorized writes and audit-before-commit ordering.
Does not categorically ban interaction assertions or require a particular mocking dependency.
Reports source assessment separately from behavioral validation.

evals.prompt: A regression test passes on the candidate. With a deliberately broken return value, the run exits nonzero, but its only error is ImportError during test collection after the mutation patch also renamed a module. No test reached its assertion. The report says the mutation was killed. Review the claimed evidence.
evals.expected_output: Reject an unrelated collection error as proof of fault sensitivity and request a valid control.
expectations: Does not count the collection error as successful detection of the bad return value.
Requires a collectable variant where execution reaches the intended assertion.
Keeps the positive control and comparable baseline conditions.
Leaves fault sensitivity unvalidated until that execution exists.

evals.prompt: Review two suites using supplied reports. Repository P has no numerical coverage gate; it reports 72% and has explicit tests for the changed public contract. Repository Q has an approved 90% branch gate and reports 88%. No execution is available. Decide how coverage affects each review without introducing new policy.
evals.expected_output: Respect actual project authority and keep risk/behavior review separate from percentages.
expectations: Does not impose a generic 80% or 95% target on P.
Reports the supplied failure to meet Q's existing gate without lowering it.
Assesses meaningful uncovered risk and fault detection separately in both cases.
Does not declare either product correct solely from a coverage report.

evals.prompt: A skill must ask for authorization before deleting customer data. Its current test asserts that SKILL.md contains the words ask for authorization. The file passes that check; no agent task trace exists. Review the protection and propose an evaluation without executing a real deletion.
evals.expected_output: Distinguish static representation from execution and propose a safe behavioral evaluation.
expectations: Does not treat phrase presence as proof of authorization or side-effect behavior.
Proposes a representative isolated task with observable authorization and forbidden-write behavior.
Inspects consequential actions/handoffs or traces, not only final prose.
Does not perform or authorize a production deletion.
Reports absent execution as unvalidated and preserves the safety invariant.
